name: Pfarrkirche St. Andreas
kurzbeschreibung: The Parish Church of St. Andrew in Kitzbühel impresses with Gothic hall architecture, sumptuous baroque sacred art, and its iconic pairing with the Liebfrauenkirche.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Parish Church of St. Andrew (Stadtpfarrkirche St. Andreas) in Kitzbühel is one of the most prominent Gothic sacred structures in the Tyrolean Unterland. Picturesquely situated on a gentle knoll overlooking the historic old town, it forms a striking architectural ensemble together with the adjacent Liebfrauenkirche and the historic churchyard, defining the skyline of the famed alpine town for centuries. Built between 1435 and 1506 as a three-aisled late Gothic hall church, the building was splendidly refurbished in the baroque style during the 17th and 18th centuries. Inside, visitors marvel at the graceful proportions, fine stucco work by the Inntal school, richly carved altars, and expansive ceiling frescoes painted by Bavarian master Matthäus Günther.

Route & Requirements

The church is reached within a five-minute stroll from Kitzbühel's town centre via the historic stone steps or gently rising paved pathways. The visit requires no physical effort and is suitable for elderly travellers and families with pushchairs. The sanctuary is step-free. Allow thirty to forty-five minutes to admire the church interior, the ornate side chapels, and the evocative cemetery with its masterfully crafted wrought-iron grave crosses. Visiting is restricted during religious services to respect worshippers.

Visiting & Getting There

Kitzbühel enjoys convenient rail connections via Kitzbühel Hauptbahnhof with direct trains from Innsbruck, Salzburg, and Munich. From the railway station or Hahnenkamm train stop, the church is a pleasant ten-minute walk away. Drivers will find municipal car parks nearby, such as the Pfarrau parking area. The parish church is open daily throughout the year with free admission. Voluntary contributions toward the church preservation are gratefully accepted.

Tips

Take time to admire the ornate baroque Rosary Chapel featuring its gilded wood-carved altar. Adjacent stands the fortress-like tower of the Liebfrauenkirche, home to the Kaiserin bell cast in 1845, renowned as one of the finest-sounding bells in Tyrol. The church terrace also provides sweeping panoramas toward the Kitzbüheler Horn and the legendary Hahnenkamm Streif downhill course. Look out for sacred organ recitals held in the church during the summer season.
